title: Triplon dynamics from partial Kondo screening in frustrated heavy-fermion systems
authors: Hiroki Nakahara, Masahito Mochizuki, Rintaro Eto
abstract: The partially disordered (PD) phase, in which magnetically ordered and Kondo-screened sites coexist, has been proposed as a possible ground state of geometrically frustrated heavy-fermion systems. We investigate its dynamical properties in the half-filled periodic Anderson model on a triangular lattice by calculating the dynamical spin susceptibility within the random-phase approximation built on a self-consistent Hartree-Fock solution. We show that successive quantum phase transitions from the Kondo-insulating phase to the PD phase and to a magnetically ordered phase are driven by the condensation of triplon modes originating predominantly from the Kondo-screened sites. In the PD phase, magnons and triplons coexist and hybridize, leading to characteristic level repulsion in the excitation spectrum. These results reveal how triplet excitations evolve into collective magnetic modes across the successive phase transitions and highlight the dynamical interplay between magnetic order and Kondo screening in frustrated heavy-fermion systems.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes the complex ground state of frustrated heavy-fermion systems using the PAM on a triangular lattice. It shows that the Partially Disordered (PD) phase is characterized by coexisting magnetic and Kondo-screened regions, with transitions driven by triplon condensation. Crucially, the analysis predicts that the PD state is unstable and evolves into a larger, nine-sublattice magnetic order.
main_problem: The study investigates the dynamical properties and stability of the Partially Disordered (PD) phase, a state where magnetically ordered and Kondo-screened sites coexist, in frustrated heavy-fermion systems.
main_result: The transition into the PD phase is driven by triplon condensation, and the PD state itself is unstable toward a larger, nine-sublattice magnetic order, which is revealed by the hybridization of magnon and triplon modes.
method: The analysis employs the Random-Phase Approximation (RPA) built upon a self-consistent Hartree-Fock (SCHF) mean-field solution to study collective excitations.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using the Periodic Anderson Model (PAM) on a triangular lattice, designed to capture the competition between Kondo screening and RKKY interactions in heavy-fermion compounds.
key_observables: Dynamical spin susceptibility, collective excitations (magnons and triplons), and the static RPA susceptibility divergence.
important_parameters: Hybridization strength ($V$), lattice geometry (triangular lattice), and the degree of magnetic order.
main_assumptions: The framework relies on the SCHF+RPA approach, which treats quantum fluctuations perturbatively around a static mean-field saddle point.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the PD state, phase diagrams showing transitions (e.g., KI to PD), and the energy spectra showing magnon-triplon hybridization and mode softening.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the PD phase via SCHF, then using RPA to analyze the excitations, demonstrating the triplon-driven transitions, and finally using free energy comparisons and excitation analysis to predict the instability of the PD state toward a nine-sublattice order.
why_interesting: The detailed study of collective excitations (magnons/triplons) and their hybridization across quantum phase transitions provides a rich model for understanding emergent quantum dynamics in strongly correlated materials, relevant to understanding complex many-body ground states.
